I tried both. The inline version feels more natural to me — I click "Edit details," the fields open up right there on the card, I fix the title to "CSS Grid Guide," save, and it updates in place. The pop-up one works fine too, but for a quick correction I like staying on the card rather than having a window take over the screen. So let's go with the inline one.

On the boundary — mostly yes. It makes sense that the site icon and preview image stay tied to the actual page, since those come from the page itself. But I wouldn't want the address locked down completely. Every so often I'll have saved the wrong link, or a link with extra tracking junk on the end, and I'd want to fix the address itself rather than delete and start over. So I'd say: title and description are the everyday edits, but being able to correct the address should be possible too when I open a bookmark to edit it.

And just so it's on your radar for when we get there — editing is also where I'll eventually want to add my own labels and a personal note to a bookmark. Not asking for that today, just flagging it's part of the same "open a bookmark and adjust it" idea in my head.
